## 

## The Public Request Form URL {#the-public-request-form-url}

The public request form instructors will use to make their requests is located at: [https://www.pcc.edu/library/instruction-request/](https://www.pcc.edu/library/instruction-request/)  

## Signing into the Instruction Request Dashboard:  {#signing-into-the-instruction-request-dashboard:}

Sign into the Instruction Request Dashboard by clicking the blue button labeled “Sign in with PCC account” and using your PCC username and password at: [https://www.pcc.edu/library/instruction-requests/public/dashboard](https://www.pcc.edu/library/instruction-requests/public/dashboard)   
![][image1]

## Instruction Request Dashboard Homepage {#instruction-request-dashboard-homepage}

After you sign in, you’ll see the dashboard, where you can access information about requests, see instruction requests that have been assigned to and accepted by you, create new requests, and view system statistics. 

### Top-left column: “Assigned” Box: {#top-left-column:-“assigned”-box:}

The top box in the left-hand column is where you’ll see instruction requests that have been assigned to you. **Tip:** These are requests you haven’t yet accepted or rejected, so they’ll need further action from you if they are in this box. You can access the full request to accept, reject, and/or view and edit the full details of the request by clicking on the blue “edit” icon to the left of the instructor name. 

### ![][image2]

### 

### Bottom-left column: “Accepted” Box: {#bottom-left-column:-“accepted”-box:}

The bottom box in the left column is where you’ll see instruction requests that have been accepted by you. **Tip:** These are requests you have accepted, but they’ll need further action from you to successfully schedule them on Google Calendar if they are in this box. You can access the full request view and edit the full details of the request by clicking on the blue “edit” icon in the right action column. **Tip:** Learn more about scheduling accepted requests with Google Calendar at the section: [Scheduling an Instruction Request with the Google Calendar Function](#scheduling-an-instruction-request-with-the-google-calendar-function)![][image3]

### Right column: “Recently Received Request” Box: {#right-column:-“recently-received-request”-box:}

In the right column is the “Recently Received Request” box. You’ll see the most recently received requests in this area. **Tip:** These are the most recently received requests to the system for everyone overall. They may not be requests for you. You can see the full details of the recent requests by clicking on the blue “edit” icon in the right action column.

### ![][image4]

### Top box: Status: {#top-box:-status:}

This is an at-a-glance summary of the tables, showing assigned, accepted, received, and completed requests. **NOTE:** The status icons and numbers are not clickable. 

### ![][image5]

### Creating new instruction requests {#creating-new-instruction-requests}

If you want to create a new request from the dashboard, you can click the green button in the footer of the “Recently Received Requests” table. **Tip:** Learn more about creating requests that have not been submitted via the public form  in the section: [“Create a new request (not received through the public form)](#create-a-new-request-\(not-received-through-the-public-form\))”.

![][image6]

### Change Dashboard to Dark Mode {#change-dashboard-to-dark-mode}

You can change the dashboard from “light” mode to “dark” mode if desired by clicking the “moon” icon in the upper left corner:  
![][image7]

Here’s what dark mode looks like (click the “sun” icon in the upper right corner to return to light mode):  
![][image8]

### Footer: Report an Issue with the Instruction Request Dashboard; Access this training document; and access the public form:  {#footer:-report-an-issue-with-the-instruction-request-dashboard;-access-this-training-document;-and-access-the-public-form:}

The footer of the back end of the Instruction Request Form platform contains three links:

![][image9]

* **Documentation:** You can [access this training document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AgxpgeGckkmmjQIhPy-2eLhVfY-gxvEYULZwGdW8JwQ/edit?usp=sharing) at any time from this link in the footer.  
* **Report an issue:** You can [access this form to report an issue](https://forms.gle/spH4ueJxhjv8LTD17) with the Instruction Request form from this link in the footer.  
* **Public form:** You can quickly [access the public Instruction Request form](https://www.pcc.edu/library/instruction-request/) from this link in the footer. 

## Dashboard Navigation {#dashboard-navigation}

### How to return to the dashboard:  {#how-to-return-to-the-dashboard:}

When using any of the navigation areas below you can return to the dashboard (aka “Home” in the screenshot above) by clicking “Instruction Requests Dashboard” in the navigation bar.   
![][image10]

### 

### Manage Campus Request Notifications (top navigation): {#manage-campus-request-notifications-(top-navigation):}

#### View Campuses {#view-campuses}

**“Campuses” in the top navigation** is where you can assign librarians to receive notifications when new instruction requests are received for each campus location. Click the green edit button in the right-hand “Action” column to add or remove librarians from each campus location. 

### ![][image11]

#### Edit campus {#edit-campus}

Edit the campus name; campus code; Google calendar ID (this “ID” connects the campus  Google calendar to the campus in the IR form so instruction can be scheduled in Google Calendar via the IR Form–more on this below); and librarians to be notified when a new request is received, or an assigned request is rejected. 

![][image12]

##### How to find and add a Google calendar ID {#how-to-find-and-add-a-google-calendar-id}

If you need to add or change the Google Calendar ID for a campus calendar, here’s how you find it and apply it: 

* Find the three dot menu next to the Google Calendar from which you need the calendar ID:

![][image13]

* Click on the “Settings” Menu, then scroll down to the “Integrate Calendar” heading and look for the “Calendar ID” field (it will look like an email address, though it may be quite long):

  ![][image14]

* Copy/paste the Calendar ID for the appropriate calendar and paste it into the “Google Calendar ID” field. Then click the green “Save” button to save the new calendar to the campus.

![][image15]

### Manage Librarian Profiles (top navigation): {#manage-librarian-profiles-(top-navigation):}

**“Librarians” in the top navigation** is where you can manage all the librarian users in the system. You can add a new librarian to the system using the green “Add Librarian” button in the upper-right corner. You can edit or delete an existing librarian by using the green “edit” and red “delete” buttons in the “Action” column.  
![][image16]

**NOTE:** New librarians need to be manually added to this system with their PCC username even if they already have a PCC account. This is a separate, manually added account that must match the PCC username for login to work correctly. 

#### Edit a librarian profile and view all instruction assigned to a librarian {#edit-a-librarian-profile-and-view-all-instruction-assigned-to-a-librarian}

You can edit a librarian profile and view all the instruction requests assigned to a librarian by clicking the green “edit” button on that librarian’s entry. Edit the entry as needed and click the green “save” button to save changes. View all the instruction requests assigned to a librarian under the heading: “Instruction Requests for \[Librarian Name\]”.![][image17]

#### Label a librarian as a “Scheduler” {#label-a-librarian-as-a-“scheduler”}

Click the “Is Scheduler” box in a librarian’s profile to indicate that the librarian is a campus “scheduler”. Once the entry is saved, that librarian will see a “scheduler” indicator to the left of their name in the top right corner. **NOTE:** Making a librarian a “scheduler” only changes the indicator they see at the top of their screen. There are currently no other permissions or separate functions associated with a “scheduler” account. “Librarian” accounts can perform the same functions as “scheduler” accounts. (Future versions of this platform plan to have more features based around different roles, but this is not currently the case.) ![][image18]

### View and Manage instructor information (top navigation): {#view-and-manage-instructor-information-(top-navigation):}

**“Instructors” in the top navigation** stores information for each instructor who submits a request. Every time an instructor submits a request, the system looks for their email and adds them if they’re new (i.e. there should not be duplicates). You can edit instructor information using the green “edit” button in the “Action” column.

![][image19]

### 

#### Edit an instructor profile and view all instruction requested by an instructor {#edit-an-instructor-profile-and-view-all-instruction-requested-by-an-instructor}

You can edit an instructor profile and view all the instruction requested by that instructor by clicking the green “edit” button on that instructor’s entry. Edit the entry as needed and click the green “save” button to save changes. View all the instruction requests from that instructor under the heading: “Instruction Requests by this instructor”.  
![][image20]

### View All Instruction Requests (top navigation) {#view-all-instruction-requests-(top-navigation)}

**To access a full list of all request information available in the system, go to “Instruction Requests” in the top navigation.** 

![][image21]

This is also where you can edit, delete, view the full details, and even create an instruction request if you need to add a request that hasn’t been submitted by the public form. Use the red edit button next to a request to edit it; the red “trashcan” button to delete it; and the green “create new request” button to create a new request. **Tip:** Learn more about creating requests that have not been submitted via the public form  in the section: [“Create a new request (not received through the public form)](#create-a-new-request-\(not-received-through-the-public-form\))”.

#### 

#### Quick Filters: “My Requests”; “Expiring Received”; and “Rejected Requests”  {#quick-filters:-“my-requests”;-“expiring-received”;-and-“rejected-requests”}

There are three buttons at the top of the full instruction request list that can help you quickly filter the list based on what you need to see. 

![][image22]

* **My Requests:** Click the teal “My Requests”  button to view all the requests assigned to you.   
* **Expiring Received:** Click the orange “Expiring Received” button to view all the requests whose instruction date is 14 days away (or less).   
* **Rejected Requests:** Click the purple “Rejected Requests” button to view all requests that have been rejected after initial assignment.   
* **Clear filters:** Click the red and white “clear filters” button to remove any filters.   
* **Top of column filters:** You can also use the filters at the top of each column to filter what the table displays.

#### Editing an Instruction Request {#editing-an-instruction-request}

If needed, you can edit the fields of any instruction request on the “Manage Instruction Request” page for that request. You can get to this page using the green “edit” icon next to any of the instruction requests on the main dashboard or the full instruction requests page. 

**To edit a request:![][image23]**

1. Click the blue “Edit Fields” button on the right side of the “Request summary” to edit any fields below the summary area. **NOTE:** You do not need to use the “Edit Fields” button to change fields in the “Status” area or accept/reject or schedule a request. “Edit fields” should only be used if you need to edit information about the original request data.  
   1.  **TIP:** Learn more about accepting, rejecting and scheduling a request in the section:  [“How to Assign, Accept, and Schedule Requests”.](#how-to-assign,-accept,-and-schedule-requests)  
2. Edit any fields necessary.  
3. Click the green “Save” button to make sure your changes have been saved

##### Request Summary {#request-summary}

This section summarizes the request with: the instruction date; assigned librarian; campus; class name; status (received, assigned, etc); Instructor; number of students; and duration of instruction. It also contains the buttons that allow you to edit and save a request 

![][image24]

#### Edit Locking on Instruction Requests {#edit-locking-on-instruction-requests}

This feature prevents two or more users from editing or deleting a request simultaneously. When a user edits a request, it becomes locked in the system. There’s a timer on the instruction request table that checks every 30 seconds to update the status of locked requests. Hovering on the lock icon will give you the name of who is editing the request. 

![][image25]

![][image26]

##### Edit Page Inactivity Timer on Instruction Requests {#edit-page-inactivity-timer-on-instruction-requests}

On the edit screen, there’s a timer (currently set to 2 minutes, which resets when you perform an action on the page) that checks for user activity. If there’s no activity detected, the user gets a warning 30 seconds before the time runs out, and again before they are redirected to the instruction requests table page.

![][image27]

### Create a new request (not received through the public form) {#create-a-new-request-(not-received-through-the-public-form)}

Click the green Create new request button on the upper right of the full instruction list page to create a new instruction request.   
![][image28]

#### New Request Creation Page {#new-request-creation-page}

This is a back-end version of the public form, which you can use for quickly creating new requests without leaving the application to use the public form.   
![][image29]

#### Select Existing Instructor {#select-existing-instructor}

If the instructor has previously submitted a request, you can find them by clicking on the indigo button labeled “Select from existing instructors” and fill in their information. 

![][image30]

Enter part of the name of the instructor to find them in the list, then click “Select” to enter their information onto the back end request  form automatically. 

![][image31]

## How to Assign, Accept, and Schedule Requests {#how-to-assign,-accept,-and-schedule-requests}

### Assign Instruction to a Librarian: {#assign-instruction-to-a-librarian:}

To assign instruction to a librarian, click “edit” on the request you want to assign. You can do this from “Recently Received Requests” on the Dashboard (or from the full list of “Instruction Requests” by clicking “Instruction Requests” in the top nav). **TIP:** if you’re not seeing the “edit” button or ”Action” column in your browser view, you may need to increase the size of your browser window, or scroll over to the right.    
![][image32]

**Next, in the “Status” area on the left**: 

1. Select the “Assigned librarian” from the dropdown (i.e. the librarian to whom you want to assign instruction)   
2. This should change the “Request status” to “assigned”, but if for some reason it doesn’t, you can  select “assigned” from the “Request status” dropdown.   
3. Then click “Save”. This will send an email notification to the assigned librarian, and will move the request to their “assigned” box on their dashboard. 

![][image33]

## 

### Accepting/Rejecting Requests: {#accepting/rejecting-requests:}

You will receive an email when an instruction request is assigned to you. Click the “view request details” button in the email to view the full details of the request and accept or reject it.

#### Email Notification with “View Request Details” button: {#email-notification-with-“view-request-details”-button:}

#### ![][image34]

#### 

#### Accept and Reject buttons in Instruction Request Details in Dashboard: {#accept-and-reject-buttons-in-instruction-request-details-in-dashboard:}

When you view the request in the back end of the system after receiving your assignment email, you’ll see a green “accept” and red “reject” button at the top of the full request. Select the appropriate button.   
![][image35]

Once you have either accepted or rejected a request, it will disappear from your “Assigned to…” box on the main dashboard. **TIP:** If you’ve accepted the request, it will appear in the “Accepted by…” box on the main dashboard for easy access. 

#### What happens when a request is rejected: {#what-happens-when-a-request-is-rejected:}

If you are a  campus scheduler, you should receive an email notification when a request is rejected by the librarian you assigned it to. Below is an example of what that email will look like:  You’ll need to go back into the dashboard to reassign the request when one is rejected. 

![][image36]

### 

### Scheduling an Instruction Request with the Google Calendar Function {#scheduling-an-instruction-request-with-the-google-calendar-function}

You will see a purple “Create Google Calendar Event” button appear underneath the “Status” box on a request after you accept that request. Clicking this button will take you through the process to schedule your request on the appropriate campus Google Calendar. **TIP:** Requests must be attributed to a campus (even if that campus is “remote”) in order to be able to schedule them on Google Calendar. If you’re not seeing the ability to create a Google Calendar event, make sure to assign it to the appropriate campus, which will place the event on the correct calendar. Remote (online, scheduled meetings) instruction sessions should be added to the “Remote” campus calendar.  
![][image37]

#### “Schedule Library Instruction” form {#“schedule-library-instruction”-form}

Once you click the purple “Create Google Calendar Event” button, a form will appear with all the information needed to schedule the session on the appropriate campus Google calendar. If needed, you can edit the form fields. **NOTE:** Changing fields in this scheduling pop-up will NOT change information on the request status or any other request information. Then click “Create Google Calendar Event” to send the instruction session information to the appropriate campus calendar. 

## ![][image38]

#### View instruction session in Google Calendar {#view-instruction-session-in-google-calendar}

You can easily view the now-scheduled session by clicking the green “Open in Google Calendar” button in the “Status” area of the request. **NOTE:** You must be signed into your PCC Google Calendar to view the calendar event (if you’re signed into your personal Google account, you won’t be taken to the correct calendar event).

![][image39]

The Google Calendar invite should now appear on your calendar, and be sent to the instructor who requested the session. For instance, in the example below, Lisa Morrow is the assigned librarian and Gustavo Lanzas is the instructor who made the request, and both are included on the Google Calendar invite.    
![][image40]
